A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GenCAD by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original CAD reconstruction, image-based retrieval, and conditional and unconditional generation results in Section 5, with additional qualitative comparisons in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds sketch-conditioned experiments, architecture ablations, and a CAD-editing demonstration.

M1.justification: The four-stage CSR, contrastive encoder, diffusion-prior, and CAD-decoder procedure remains unchanged, as do its losses and selected architectures. Sketch experiments reuse this framework. Explicitly documenting prepending the SOL token clarifies decoding rather than establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds sketch-conditioned retrieval and generation alongside rendered-image conditioning. Section 3.2 describes 845,105 synthetic sketches made with Canny edges and Gaussian blur. This materially expands evaluated input conditions, although the underlying DeepCAD geometry remains unchanged and real hand-drawn sketches are not established as evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds evaluated BrepGen and ContrastCAD + RRE comparisons to DeepCAD and SkexGen, substantially expanding the principal generation comparison. BrepGen was cited but not included in this comparison in v1. The appendix comparison with One-2-3-45, Shap-E, and DreamGaussian is retained.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 revises the reported image count from 840,947 to 845,105 while retaining CAD train/validation/test counts. New experiments introduce sketch preprocessing and CSR-depth and encoder-architecture configurations. Existing training budgets, metrics, and point-sampling settings remain unchanged; the revised count does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests CSR encoder/decoder depths of two, four, and six layers and compares ResNet-10/18/34 with ViT for retrieval. These provide quantitative architecture analyses absent from v1. Figure 13 also adds an Onshape feature-editing case study. Existing sequence-length analysis and failure examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report retrieval repetitions of 1000, 10, 3, and 3 for the four candidate-set sizes, with the same plus/minus reporting practice. New sketch and encoder-ablation rows extend that practice without introducing new uncertainty procedures, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing reconstruction, image-retrieval, generation, and FID values are retained. New sketch-generation results are COV 82.59, MMD 1.33, JSD 3.53, and FID 0.32; sketch retrieval at 2048 candidates is 60.77 ± 0.75. Added competitor rows give BrepGen the lowest reported MMD/JSD, 1.05/1.22. Tables 5–6 add architecture-ablation outcomes.

T1.justification: The CAD representation, objectives, and mathematical evaluation definitions are substantively retained. Replacing the parameter-vector length notation with Np is equivalent for the fixed-dimensional representation. Omitting the explicit standard Chamfer-distance formula does not establish a changed metric. Neither version supplies new theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction's main contribution and the conclusion broaden GenCAD from image-conditioned generation to both image- and sketch-conditioned generation. The abstract also shifts its superiority claim from precision and modifiability to conditional and unconditional generation. Reconstruction and the greater-than-15-fold retrieval claim remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking BrepGen's stronger MMD/JSD and the sketch model's higher FID to diversity tradeoffs, plus reasons for selecting four CSR layers and ResNet-18. These explanations accompany new evidence rather than establishing causal mechanisms. Existing limitations concerning vocabulary, invalid geometry, and clean isometric inputs remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents sketch creation and the ablation ViT's six attention layers, 16 heads, and patch size 32, and clarifies SOL-token handling. Appendix C removes component-class and normalization snippets. Core training and hardware details are retained, with the old Appendix D moved to E. The encoder ablation's image-versus-sketch labeling remains ambiguous.

R1.justification: v2 removes the neural-representation survey subsection and associated references, while adding works including DiffCAD, ContrastCAD, ViT, volumetric design, and reverse engineering. Section 5.2 now acknowledges existing CAD-model retrieval and confines the claimed gap to CAD-program retrieval. The overall generative-CAD positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, one related-work subsection is removed, terminology and grammar receive localized edits, and pseudocode is shortened. A new ablation appendix shifts the training-details appendix lettering. Most explanatory prose and the main section sequence are retained, so this is not an extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 substantially redesigns the title page and overview, combines the diffusion schematic's panels, and reorganizes large qualitative galleries into compact figures incorporating sketches. It expands comparison tables, adds two ablation tables and an editing figure, and adds a sketch FID bar. These are extensive visual changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support: Appendix D supplies previously missing architecture ablations, Table 3 broadens competitor coverage and reveals performance tradeoffs, and Figure 13 demonstrates the claimed editability. Synthetic-sketch experiments provide evidence for the expanded input scope, while reorganized figures improve readability. Broad superiority wording and ambiguous image/sketch ablation labels limit precision, but do not outweigh these substantial gains in validation and assessability.
